In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relativistic treatment of the 2p-2h electromagnetic response function is mandatory in order to obtain a correct description of the MEC effects.
the MEC effects in R T are small, and that they are of the same size and of similar nature as the relativistic corrections to the one-body current operator.

the MEC contributions to R T are very significant in the quasielastic region, where they can be up to 50% of the impulse approximation, but that the relative impact of these corrections decreases as the momentum transfer increases, so that at high Q 2, the 2p-2h MEC contributions to the nuclear response become negligible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 2p-2h response is a small correction to the one-body nuclear response.

the relativistic MEC contribution is of the same order as that obtained in the non-relativistic approach, but with a different relative importance of the various components.
